text:
The old planks of the Blackwood Bay pier hummed a low, unsettling frequency under David Vance's worn boots. It wasn't an earthquake, not really, but the persistent vibration was enough to make the distant gulls sound off-key, their cries a ragged fringe against the leaden sky. Beneath the pilings, the brackish water lay unnaturally still, a thin, iridescent film spreading slowly from the derelict trawlers tied to their moorings, a sheen like an oil slick reflecting the dullness above, hinting at something vital seeping away from the world.

He wasn't sure if the tremor was just in his head, or if it was another symptom of Blackwood Bay's slow unraveling. The whispers had started a week ago, a low current beneath the town's usual gossip, detailing how Old Man Thorne, the last of the family that practically built this town, found his accounting books not just 'missing a few pages,' but subtly rearranged, figures shifted, entire ledgers appearing emptied of their meticulous entries, as if a ghost had been trying to balance the books and failed. Or succeeded, depending on whose side you were on, or what unseen hand was pulling the strings.

Vance pulled his trench coat tighter against the damp, creeping cold. Strange money, strange ground, strange town. It all led back to the docks, where the Thorne fortune had started, and where, he suspected, it was now trying to die a quiet, unnatural death. The film on the water, he decided, wasn't just oil. It was a shroud. He needed to talk to Thorne's estranged nephew, the one who always seemed to know more than he let on, and who usually frequented the greasy spoon by the old lighthouse.
